title: Witch of Izalith
snippet:
Witch of Izalith -  Dark Souls - character - trivia 
 trivia : The name of the Witch is literally **Izalith**, as stated by Quelana in the Japanese version, where she calls the Witch "my mother Izalith".
During her dialogue, Quelana mentions that most humans are unable to perceive her, and implies that they absolutely cannot, so long as she actively does not want them to.
Despite herself being consumed by the Chaos Flame, Izalith was partially successful in replicating the First Flame. Not only does Chaos generate life, it also has its own fire-linking quality, wherein a demon Champion is destined to rekindle it, becoming the Demon Prince. This system parallels the prophecy of the Chosen Undead and their becoming a Lord of Cinder.

title: Witch of Izalith
snippet:
Witch of Izalith -  Dark Souls - character - lead 
 lead : The **Witch of Izalith** or simply **Izalith** (イザリス) is a mentioned character in *Dark Souls*. She is also mentioned in *Dark Souls II*, although by that time her name is lost to history and only her nickname of "mother of pyromancy" remains.

A legendary fire sorcerer who found one of the four Lord Souls, she helped bring an end to the Age of Ancients and the rule of the dragons to establish the Age of Fire, and established an underground civilization named after her. She had many daughters, nicknamed the "Daughters of Chaos", which included Quelaag, Quelana and "The Fair Lady", as well as a son. By the time of the game's events, her magical experiments backfired, fusing her soul and two of her daughters' into a new horrible being, the Bed of Chaos. Although the Bed was eventually slain by the Chosen Undead and its soul fed to the Lordvessel, fragments of the Witch's soul survived.

Izalith's pyromancies were said to only be known to old Master Salaman, mentioned by Quelana as being her pupil, now lost to time. Even as her pyromancies themselves were all but history, her cautionary tales on the dangers of the flame were passed down through generations of pyromancers.

title: Quelana of Izalith
snippet:
Quelana of Izalith -  Dark Souls - character - dark_souls_i 
 dark_souls_i : Quelana was originally a "flame witch" who used fire sorcery. When Izalith was consumed and the demons infested the city, she fled and became the creator of pyromancy. It is unknown whether the knowledge of fire sorcery was forgotten by her or whether she created pyromancy as a safer version of it. Quelana passed on her knowledge to Salaman, who in turn passed on his knowledge of pyromancy to the people of the Great Swamp.

According to a developer interview, Quelana and the other Daughters of Chaos are a different species than humans, despite being similar in appearance. Her in-game model may not reflect her "canon" appearance, with pale, ash-colored skin, as seen in the opening cutscene and achievement art.

title: Chaos Witch Quelaag
snippet:
Chaos Witch Quelaag -  Dark Souls - boss - lore 
 lore : She is the Fair Lady's older sister. When their mother, the Witch of Izalith along with their other two sisters became the Bed of Chaos, she and her sister became half demon spiders.

Quelaag and her sister stationed just outside the Demon Ruins, in a fraction of Blighttown that became known as Quelaag's Domain. The two started to breed demon insects to enlarge the demon army, by offering Humanities to the Fair Lady. People in Blighttown venerated the two witches, and gladly accepted to become hosts of the Fair Lady's eggs.

When the people were stricken by a blight, Quelaag's sister chose to absorb their pus to save their lives, which greatly weakened and blinded her while making any further eggs incapable of holding life. Quelaag remained by her side as her guardian and a hunter of undead to gather the humanity necessary to sustain her sister as a Fire Keeper.

title: Quelana of Izalith
snippet:
Quelana of Izalith -  Dark Souls - character - lead 
 lead : **Quelana of Izalith** (クラーナ) is a character and merchant in *Dark Souls*.

Found in the swamp at the bottom of Blighttown if special conditions are met, she is one of the Witch of Izalith's "Daughters of Chaos", and acts as a seller and trainer of pyromancies.

She is voiced by Jenny Funnel, who also voiced the Darkmoon Knightess in the same game, Yuria and Selen Vinland in *Demon's Souls*, Annalise and Iosefa in *Bloodborne*, and Karla and the Old Woman of Londor in *Dark Souls III*.

title: Quelana of Izalith
snippet: Following the destruction of the Bed of Chaos, Quelana appears to have returned to Izalith, or what remains of it, at some point. Within the Demon Ruins, now neighbouring the Catacombs of Carthus, Quelana's pyromancy tome is found on a corpse clutching onto what seems like the petrified corpse of her sister. If these two fossils are indeed those of Quelana and the Fair Lady, it would show that Quelana ultimately ended her self-imposed exile to be reunited with her last extant sister, in the final hours of her life.

title: Lore
snippet: The Age of Fire began prosperous and rich, but soon the fires started to go out again and with them the power of the Lords. In an effort to prolong Age of Fire, the Witch of Izalith tried to recreate the First Flame, but the experiment failed and a flame called "The Flame of Chaos" is created instead, which transformed her into the Bed of Chaos and many creatures into the demons that roam Lordran. Her children are transformed as well, with her son becoming a flame demon called Ceaseless Discharge and her daughter Quelaag and her sister partially into spiders. Her followers stay loyal to her, however, and become known as the "Witches of Chaos". Only her daughter, Quelana, escaped the fire and becomes the mother of pyromancy. This being said, Mother Izalith did eventually *succeed* in stabilizing the Chaos Flame with 2 of her sisters.

snippet:

 the_witch_of_izalith : The Witch used the power of her Lord Soul to weave great storms of fire against the Everlasting Dragons. She passed fragments of this soul to her children, the Daughters of Chaos, and her only son. Like her children, she had ashen skin and blue lips, though she stood much taller than them and seems to be of identical height to the staves her children used for flame sorcery.

As the fires faded, she tried to create a new flame to replicate the First Flame, but it backfired and ended up costing her life, and gave birth to the race of demons. Her children were also corrupted, except for Quelana, who taught a flame manipulating art to a human and became the mother of pyromancy. Many years later, the demons began to die out, as the flame of chaos began to fade much like the First Flame did.

title: Demon (lore)
snippet: At one point Izalith, aiming to gain greater sway over the Flame of Chaos, lost all control of the power again and never regained it: Chaos engulfed the Lord and her daughters before scorching their city with them. Izalith and her two daughters directly involved in the experiment were left permanently scarred, reduced to a monstrous lignified creature anchored in the throne room at the center of the city. Of the daughters of Izalith, few managed to escape. Quelaag and her sister's lower bodies were molded into deformed demonic spiders and the flames of chaos engulfed them but they managed to escape the city and survive on its borders, carving out a domain for themselves. The only other survivor, who managed to avoid the corruption of chaos and retain a normal body, was Quelana, who remained in self-imposed exile around the ruins of her country for centuries.

title: Smouldering Lake
snippet: This was once the home to the daughters of the Witch of Izalith and the demons born from the Flame of Chaos. Unlike the First Flame, which is tied to the souls of the undead, the faded Flame of Chaos was tied to the souls of the demons, and so the lifeless bodies of Capra, Taurus, Asylum and a single Centipede Demon can be found strewn throughout the ruins and piled high near the Old Demon King, one of the last remaining demons of old. A petrified arachnoid body, resembling Quelaag's Sister, lies within the ruins, where a humanoid corpse holds the Quelana Pyromancy Tome, indicated that the sisters lived here at one point.

snippet: Desperate to ensure that their Age of Fire continued, and afraid of the coming Dark, the Lords did everything they could to keep the First Flame lit. title: Quelana of Izalith
snippet:
Quelana of Izalith -  Dark Souls - character - strategy 
 strategy : Quelana has an unlimited amount of pyromancies at her disposal. She seems to prefer Great Fireball and Fire Tempest the most. Both are very powerful if they connect, but have slow start-ups, allowing players to go for the backstab if they are close enough. Quelana may deal high damage but is physically very weak. Quelana is also just as susceptible to poison as the player is; one can choose to attack her and have her wade into the swamp surrounding her, leading to a slow death. Finally, the Infested Barbarians can also damage her heavily should they chase the player to that point.

title: Quelaag's Domain
snippet:

Inside is the arena where Quelaag is fought and where her sister nests by her bonfire. The second Bell of Awakening is also found immediately after the fight with Quelaag.

title: Chaos Witch Quelaag
snippet:
Chaos Witch Quelaag -  Dark Souls - boss - strategy 
 strategy : A relatively easy way to beat this boss is to be human and summon Maneater Mildred, whose summon sign is right outside the Fog Door. Let Mildred distract Quelaag and stay away from her lava attack, as this is certain death. When away from her, pick off her health with ranged attacks, while Mildred tanks. This way Quelaag should be dead within a short period of time.

Another easy way to kill her is to get any halberd with a vertical light attack, such as the Great Scythe or Gargoyle's Halberd, and then repeatedly hitting Quelaag's human part. When aimed properly, she will stagger every time the attack connects, interrupting whatever she's doing. This can be repeated to prevent her from attacking at all.

There is a spot between the stairs on the far side of the arena and the wall where Quelaag is unable to reach the player, at which point she can safely be killed from a distance using ranged attacks.

title: Chaos Witch Quelaag
snippet:
Chaos Witch Quelaag -  Dark Souls - boss - notes 
 notes : Hitting her human body is a critical hit (Double Damage ignoring defense) that will stun her instantly.
The Black Knight weapons will do extra damage against Quelaag.
It is possible to summon Maneater Mildred for this battle provided she was defeated in Blighttown. Mildred has a large amount of health and can help distract the boss whilst the player attacks from a distance or heals.
Running on the right-hand side of the swamp to Quelaag's domain will let the player ignore all enemies with ease, which can speed up the process of retrying the bossfight.
Very rarely, Quelaag will actually jump at the player from a considerable distance. If this connects, it will knock the player down regardless of their poise, and inflict massive damage.
**Further, she can follow up with a lava attack, resulting in an almost guaranteed death to an already injured player.

snippet:
Zullie the Witch -  Dark Souls III - character - theories 
 theories : It's possible that Zullie shares a connection with Karla, the witch imprisoned in Irithyll Dungeon, perhaps even being her mother.

For one, the jailed witch is described as a "spurned child of the abyss", and Alva, Zullie's companion, gains the title of "Seeker of the Spurned" in *Dark Souls III* specifically. He also invades at the entrance of the forsaken dungeon, and his corpse is found right outside her cell should his phantom be killed by the player. Most curiously, one of the two sorceries that Karla can teach from the beginning is Dark Edge, which is said to be passed from mother to daughter. The apparition of Zullie summoned by the Judicator Giants also seems to use a stronger variant of that same spell, one that can't be obtained in-game, possibly lending more credence to the existence of a familial connection between the two witches.

Yet in spite of her confidence in the practice of witchcraft, she still had a need for hiding that part of her, especially when traveling. For that purpose she used a long veil.

title: Velka, Goddess of Sin
snippet: Velka is a peculiar deity who is addressed as a "witch" and "heretic deity"; although she remains in the Anor Londo pantheon, her ideas and practices deviate from dominant tenets. She is involved with secret rituals capable of denying the use of magic in an area, as well as sacrificial rituals for creating mystical rings, and the talismans crafted with her hair are used to cast miracles drawing not upon faith but intelligence, implying that the goddess favors the latter among her followers. Velka is nonetheless greatly influential in the world of men and of gods, and is versed in arts both new and old, given her interest in the most recent sorceries.

 dark_souls : Elizabeth is a member of the Mushroom People of the adjacent woods. She is a master of golden sorcery and the guardian of Oolacile's Sanctuary, as well as Princess Dusk's wet nurse. The two appear to be very close, as the princess will tell her about the Chosen Undead, who rescued her from her imprisonment in the Golden Crystal Golem. She is also adept in medicine, treating mushrooms into potent restorative items.

When the Chosen Undead is dragged into the past by Manus, she is able to instantly recognize them due to the stories of Dusk. She begs for their help and shares her insight and wares with them. She speaks of Knight Artorias, and how he would fall to the Abyss, and of Marvelous Chester, another man from a faraway time who she describes as being odious.

snippet: At some point the creatures that found the Lord Souls near the First Flame underground and developed their powers emerged to the surface with the intention of exterminating the Dragons and conquer the world for themselves.  lore : In the Age of Ancients, the Witch of Izalith and her Daughters of Chaos wove great and powerful firestorms. At the time, the Witch and her followers were powerful flame sorcerers who lived in the city of Izalith. Blacksmiths of the ancient city crafted powerful weapons using Chaos arts. Thus, during the earliest known ages of the world, Chaos developed its reputation as a powerful force.

Eventually, the Witch of Izalith attempted to duplicate the First Flame. What she instead produced was a twisted being of chaotic fire: the Bed of Chaos, source of all demons. Several of the Witch's daughters were transformed into chaos demons, and her son became the monstrous Ceaseless Discharge.

snippet:
Demon (lore) -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : After The Witch of Izalith found an immense and powerful Lord Soul near the First Flame, she pooled her and her daughters' newfound strength into aiding fellow Lords in winning the war against the Dragons and built their civilization underground. They continued to experiment with the power of fire and souls; at a certain point, driven by ambition and arrogance, Izalith, using her own Lord Soul as a basis, tried to recreate the First Flame, the primordial force that had brought life into the world. This, however, was not entirely successful, resulting in the Flame of Chaos, an unstable power that the witch was unable to control. She was initially consumed by it and became a beast of chaos fire along with two of her daughters: the "Bed of Chaos". This creature, fueled by the power of the Flame of Chaos, became a seedbed for a new life form: Demons.

title: Demon Firesage
snippet: lore : The Firesage Demons were the first generation of demons spawned from the Bed of Chaos, the entity that appeared following the attempt of the Witch of Izalith to make a power similar to the First Flame using her Lord Soul. The attempt was successful and she create the Flame of Chaos but Izalith and her powerful soul became a seedbed for a new lifeform: the mother and source of all demons. While the very first demon, Ceaseless Discharge, was a monstrous and unstable mutation of a son of Izalith while her newly created Flame of Chaos was still unstable, the Firesage Demon is one of the demons that were generated after Izalith and her daughters managed to stabilize their new flame, thus gaining a more defined body and control over the power of chaos inside its body. The Lords feared the Dark, and sought to prolong the Age of Fire. The Witch of Izalith attempted to create a new flame. However, this new Chaos Flame grew out of control and consumed the Witch of Izalith and many of her children, soon forming into a creation known as the Bed of Chaos, which consumed Izalith and mutated most of the Witch of Izalith's remaining children into abominable creatures, while also turning her only son into a volcanic monstrosity.  lore : The Souls of Lords were discovered by the chosen few that "came from the dark". Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight, Nito, the First of the Dead, The Witch of Izalith and the Furtive Pygmy.

Gwyn, Nito and The Witch of Izalith used the power procured from the Lord Souls to challenge the Everlasting Dragons for dominion of the world and, with the help of others, were successful in their endeavor.

The Witch of Izalith attempted to recreate her own First Flame by using her Lord Soul, but this resulted in her own demise and the creation of the Bed of Chaos, mother of all Demons, who inherited possession of the Soul.

Bequeathed Lord Soul Shards are fragments of Gwyn's Lord Soul and were bestowed as gifts. One was given to Seath the Scaleless for betraying his own kind. Another was given to the Four Kings when Lord Gwyn recognized their foresight as leaders of New Londo.

title: Demon (lore)
snippet:
Demon (lore) -  Dark Souls III - character - lead 
 lead : **Demons** are a race in the *Dark Souls* universe.

"True" Demons (labelled **Chaos Demons** in this article), are beings (some unique, others members of specific sub-species) originating from the fall of Izalith prior to *Dark Souls*, during which the Witch of Izalith lost control of her Lord Soul, causing the creation of the Flame of Chaos that twisted beings in Izalith and turned the Witch into the Bed of Chaos, a creative force that kept on endlessly making new lifeforms: Demons, which spilled from Izalith into the world. They typically have affinities for fire and/or stone.

title: Dragon
snippet:
Dragon -  Dark Souls III - character - age_of_ancients 
 age_of_ancients : In the Age of Ancients, the world was shrouded by fog, filled with grey crags and arch-trees, and ruled by the immortal Everlasting Dragons. The dragons were unmatched, but eventually, subterranean humanoids would discover a great power within the First Flame, giving them the means to challenge the dragons.

With the birth of the First Flame—the Advent of Fire—the Lords challenged the ancient dragons for dominion of the world. Lord Gwyn's mighty bolts peeled apart their stone scales. The Witch of Izalith and her Daughters of Chaos wove great firestorms, burning the Archtrees. Gravelord Nito unleashed a miasma of death and disease.

title: Salaman the Master Pyromancer
snippet:
Salaman the Master Pyromancer -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Salaman was from an era two hundred years before the events that transpired in Lordran with the arrival of the Chosen Undead. He was the first to meet Quelana of Izalith after her self-imposed exile from her homeland. He was capable of seeing her and was thus allowed to learn her pyromancy, becoming Master Pyromancer in the world of men.

He also came to be known by the title "Great Fireball", referring to the pyromancy of the same name which he ostensibly used often, learned from Quelana herself. He would later pass on his knowledge to his own pupil, Carmina, who pushed pyromancy towards a new direction.

title: Ceaseless Discharge
snippet: Unfortunately, this affected the son of Izalith too and he became the first demon to manifest itself and transformed into Ceaseless Discharge, dropping his ring in the process. The Centipede Demon spawned where it fell. As the first demon, the Flame of Chaos inside his body was still unstable, leaving it to burn him constantly. Izalith and her daughters managed to stabilize the new power they had created and began to generate the first real demons, life forms with stable bodies and capable of controlling the flame of chaos within each of them.

title: Flame of Chaos
snippet:
Flame of Chaos -  Dark Souls - storyline - lore 
 lore : The Flame of Chaos was created by the Witch of Izalith when she attempted to use her Lord Soul to recreate the First Flame. When she was unable to control it, she was consumed by it and transformed into the Bed of Chaos, mother of all Demons. Most of her children were similarly consumed and transformed into monstrosities; her daughter Quelana, however, escaped and used the Flame of Chaos to create the art of Pyromancy.

After the defeat of the Bed of Chaos at the hand of the Chosen Undead, the flames of Chaos persisted. It would eventually be discovered beneath Eleum Loyce, in the form of The Old Chaos. The Old Chaos would go on to consume many of Eleum Loyce's knights, turning them into Charred Loyce Knights, and eventually claiming the ruler of Eleum Loyce himself. The Ivory King would eventually be freed, at the bequest of his oracle Alsanna, by the Bearer of the Curse.

title: Company Captain Yorshka
snippet: At some point, after Gwyndolin had become the "Chief Deity" of the Anor Londo clan, Yorshka reached Irithyll of the Boreal Valley, the city her brother had built on the ruins of Anor Londo to house the Irithyllians, hybrids between the race of the gods of Anor Londo and humans. Here she was welcomed by Gwyndolin who formed a relationship of deep affection with his newfound sister, giving her a sacred chime and even the name Yorshka. Eventually a church was built in her name inside Irithyll—exactly where the Painted World of Ariamis was once kept— in which she was venerated as a goddess by the humans who worked in the city.

title: Lore
snippet:
Lore -  Dark Souls - storyline - the_war_of_fire 
 the_war_of_fire : With their new found power the Lords challenged the dominion of the Everlasting Dragons over the World. The Lords allied with one of the dragons, Seath the Scaleless, who sought the immortal scales of the dragons and thus betrayed his own kind. A very long and destructive war was begun by the Lords and their amassed armies. Gwyn used his powerful bolts to peel their stone scales, while the Witch of Izalith and her Daughters of Chaos wove great firestorms against them and finally the Gravelord Nito unleashed a miasma of death upon the dragons. The war was won by the Lords and the dragons were defeated. A golden Age of Fire begun as the World rebuilt under the new rule of the now as deities perceived Lords.

Just like the other Old Ones, the Lost Sinner is possessed by one of the great lords of Lordran, specifically the Witch of Izalith, as suggested by the Chaos Bug from Lost Izalith in *Dark Souls* and the Old Witch Soul she drops in NG+ (which can also be traded for a Chaos Blade), as well as having Pyromancers assist her in battle. snippet:
Stray Demon -  Dark Souls - boss - lore 
 lore : The Stray Demon is a greater demon spawned from the Bed of Chaos, the entity that appeared following the attempt of the Witch of Izalith to make a power similar to the First Flame using her Lord Soul. The attempt was successful and she create the Flame of Chaos but Izalith and her powerful soul became a seedbed for a new lifeform: the mother and source of all demons. After its birth, the Stray Demon managed to survive the war that the Silver Knights of Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight waged against its kind and at some point it was able to escape from the ruins of Lost Izalith. The demon wandered Lordran until it came to reside in the Northern Undead Asylum, the prison designed to keep Undead locked away from the rest of the world until the end of time, and that became its domain.

title: Eygil
snippet:
Eygil -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - about_their_potential_identity 
 about_their_potential_identity : Magus Eygil could also be a candidate for the identity of the Lost Sinner.

Both are connected to pyromancy, one through their active interest in granting a will to flame, the other through her connection to the Witch of Izalith, the proprieties of her Penal Handcuffs, which increase the effectiveness of pyromancies, and the presence of Pyromancers during her NG+ rematch. And though the Lost Sinner is specified to have been a woman, no pronoun is ever used to identify Eygil, meaning that their gender is unconfirmed and that they could be female as well. After all, women are subtly implied to have an innate propensity for pyromancy, as evidenced by Carmina revolutionizing the art more than her master Salaman did, or Quelana's written pyromancies only being decipherable by female pyromancers, or even Rosabeth being inherently good at the art despite wishing to be a sorcerer.

snippet:
Gwyn, Lord of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - boss - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Gwyn is one of the primordial humanoid creatures that appeared underground after the First Flame appeared, bringing life, death and disparity. He was among those who found the four Lord Souls, sources of immense power, together with Gravelord Nito, the Witch of Izalith and the Furtive Pygmy.

With the immense power of his soul, the greatest among all the Lords, Gwyn established an underground civilization, becoming its ruler and forming an army of Silver Knights. At some point Gwyn had a relationship with an unknown woman and from their union were born his firstborn son and his eldest daughter, Gwynevere.

snippet: However the flames of Chaos would not be sated, and over time the Ivory Knight was drained of his vigour and, sensing the degradation of his power he decided to plunge into Chaos' heart in an attempt to reduce its flames alone. However he was devoured by the chaos, becoming an empty husk controlled by it. title: Witch of Izalith
snippet:
Witch of Izalith -  Dark Souls - character - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : Despite the Bed of Chaos having been destroyed by a Chosen Undead, a fragment of the Flames of Chaos managed to survive and drifted to settle underground in the far north of Drangleic. Here it reformed as an expanse of fire, lava and roots and started to give birth to atrocities and monsters that cursed the region, leading people to flee in fear. Eventually the Ivory King and his knights managed to eliminate the demons that arose from the Old Chaos and drive them back into the depths. The sovereign, thanks to the power of his soul, thus built the kingdom of Eleum Loyce over that land and erected an immense cathedral, a fortress city and a Garrison Wall above the Chaos, in an attempt to contain it and its horrors with all his efforts, even going so far as to use the power of his own soul to stem his raging flames.

title: Witch of Izalith
snippet: As a last resort to stem the advance of the Chaos that couldn't be contained, the decision was made to "fling open" the ivory gates of the fortress of Eleum Loyce. Alsanna, as the heiress to her Lord's wishes and in reverence of the apocalypse, devoted herself and the power of her Dark Soul to a ritual in the hopes of appeasing the raging flame. The entire land of Eleum Loyce grew cold and lifeless, turning into a frigid expanse, in an attempt to freeze Chaos along with the entire country. The Knights of Eleum Loyce remained to watch over the Garrison Ward, faithful to the King's final order of containing the Chaos, and waited patiently for a new leader strong enough to guide them into its depths, while Alsanna remained in prayer inside the Cathedral over the depths to continue the ritual to keep the Chaos contained.

title: Witch of Izalith
snippet: At some point, a pyromancer was imprisoned inside the furthest cell of the Sinners' Rise, an isolated tower apart from the The Lost Bastille. While the Bastille was used to contain the Undead that plagued the region, this pyromancer was imprisoned and contained in an extreme manner, with Penal Handcuffs to restrain their powers and a Penal Mask with spikes pointing inward to bind and torture them, to be punished for their sins. One day the prisoner came into contact with the soul of Izalith deep inside the Lost Bastille, and a Chaos Bug similar to one Izalith had been reduced came to inhabit their body. The remnants of Izalith's will influenced the prisoner, leaving them eternally to punish themselves for the sins of her past, for trying to light a First Flame in her arrogance. Their sword became cursed with a power similar to that of the ancient Chaos Blade, symbolizing the burden of Izalith's misdeeds.
